maps.name: Whisperwood
maps.subtitle: The old pilgrim road and the old forest

props.text: West: Lanternvale. East: the Wayside Shrine, the Old Bridge and the pilgrim stair. (Someone has added: BEWARE MOSSLINGS.)
A vermilion gate, its paint flaking. A wooden tablet reads: 'Halfway. Rest your feet, not your heart.'
The Wayside lantern. A faint warmth lingers in the stone, like a hand just withdrawn.
A small stone fox wearing a red bib. Someone has left it a rice ball.
A tiny lantern made from a thimble, hung on a twig. It burns a very nibbled wick.
The Old Bridge. Someone has painted 'TOLL' on it, and someone else has added a very small sad face.
A spirit-lantern, cold and dark. The stone still remembers being warm.
The first arch of the pilgrim stair, wound tight with grey, thorned roots.
A spirit-lantern, cold and dark. The stone still remembers being warm.
A stump with a tiny ladder up its side, and a lookout post on top made of three twigs and a lot of determination.
A thimble lantern hung on a twig. A label in very careful letters says: PROPERTY OF SPRIG, ROYAL SCOUT. DO NOT BLOW OUT.
Tamsin's cottage. Strings of drying mushrooms hang under the eaves like bunting, and the doormat says WIPE YOUR SPORES.
Neat rows of leeks and turnips, and at the end a row of mushroom logs, each one labelled. 'Blewits.' 'Chanterelles.' 'Do NOT eat (Gerald).'
The Grandmother Tree. Seven people holding hands could not reach round her. Someone has tried: there are seven little ribbons tied to her bark, at seven different heights.
A small vermilion gate before the great tree. The tablet reads: 'She was here first. Be polite.'
A stone fox with a moss bib, keeping one eye on the pool and one on you.
A stone fox, very slightly smug. Someone has left it an acorn cap full of rice.
A standing stone swallowed in moss. Something is carved under it.
HERON FORD. Mind the third stone. (Underneath, in a different hand: it still wobbles. — P.)
An old ford lamp on an iron crook. The oil is fresh. Somebody still fills it.
A hollow willow stump on the bank. It smells powerfully of fish.
East across the Mossy Ford: the Heron Watch. West: the Grandmother Tree. (Someone has drawn a mossling in a crown, pointing at the ground.)
The Heron Watch tower, split open by a hundred winters and one very determined oak. A faded blue pennant still flies from the top, out of sheer stubbornness.
The Watch gate. A heron is carved in the keystone, wings spread, with moss for feathers.
The watch beacon: an iron basket on a stone plinth, full of cold, damp ash. Someone has stacked fresh kindling beside it. It hasn't caught.
The watch beacon burns tall and gold. Nobody tends it. It never seems to need it.
The watch roster: forty names in faded ink, each with a tiny painted heron. At the very bottom, in a boy's careful hand: 'Pell — keeps the fire.'
A stone bench by the beacon. On the end sits a cup of tea, still faintly warm. Tamsin's, by the mushroom painted on it.
The Kestrel Stone. From up here the old forest rolls away like a green sea, and far to the north the snowy teeth of Skyreach catch the last of the light.
A waist-high cairn of lichened stones, where riders once left word for the Heron Watch.
An enormous old tree, its roots knuckled over a boulder. A heron's nest the size of a cart sits in the crown, empty.

transitions.label: The Old Lantern Shrine
transitions.lockedText: A wall of grey, thorned roots chokes the pilgrim stair. Something huge breathes behind it.

regions.text: Whisperwood — the old pilgrim road winds east beneath the trees.
The Wayside Shrine — halfway up the pilgrim road. Its lantern is dark.
Puddlecap Hollow. Tiny tents, tiny footprints, very large hat.
The Spiders' Hollow — webs glitter between the pines.
The Grey Grove. Colour drains from everything here. Even your breath looks grey.
The Old Forest — north of the pilgrim road the trees grow older, taller and quieter. Some of them were saplings when the Shrine was young.

regions.name: Lanterncap Glade
regions.text: Lanterncap Glade. The mushrooms here glow like paper lanterns — brighter than they should — and something has strung grey webs between them.

regions.name: Tamsin's Clearing
regions.text: A clearing that smells of woodsmoke and drying mushrooms. Someone lives out here, and likes it.

regions.name: The Grandmother Tree
regions.text: The Grandmother Tree. The air under her is cool and green and very still, like the inside of a held breath.

regions.name: Mossy Hollow
regions.successText: Cold air is breathing out of the rock behind that curtain of moss — and far below, something glows. A cave!
regions.failText: A mossy hollow under the rocks. Pretty, and damp, and very green.

regions.name: The Heron Watch
regions.text: The Heron Watch — a ruined outpost of the Heronguard, swallowed by moss. Its beacon is cold.

regions.name: Kestrel Stone
regions.text: The Kestrel Stone. The whole old forest lies below you, green on green, all the way to the mountains.
